children: on Thursday announced an amendment to its existing agreement with RemeGen
to add the Chinese biotech’s next-gen dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitor RC298 in a deal worth up to $356M.

Under the agreement, the Boston, Massachusetts-based biotech will receive an exclusive license to develop and commercialize RC298 outside Greater China in exchange for $56M upfront and up to 300M in development milestone payments.
The upfront payment comprises $10M in cash and warrants to purchase 2.3M shares of Vor Bio common stock for $0.01 each, implying a total equity value of $46M based on VOR’s last closing price.
RC298 is currently undergoing early-stage development activities with RemGen targeting an investigational new drug application in China in H1 2027.
The amendment expands the companies’ existing partnership, which was established in 2025, handing the U.S. company ex-China licensing rights for another BAFF/APRIL inhibitor called telitacicept

“RC298’s differentiated long-acting profile has the potential to expand the franchise into additional autoimmune diseases and treatment settings, extending the therapeutic reach of dual BAFF/APRIL inhibition,” said Vor Bio

title: Vor Bio, RemeGen expand collaboration to add autoimmune disease therapy
